post.author: Andreas Heine
post.topic_summary: Announcing i3x2ua v1.2, an industrial OPC UA interoperability tool that progressed from protocol compliance (v1.0) to MCP tooling for AI (v1.1) to a human-friendly UI (v1.2).

comment_posted.comment_text: The sequence is right. Protocol compliance gets you to "data is technically accessible." MCP tooling gets you to "an AI agent can reason over what's there without a human hardcoding every query": the agent can ask what endpoints exist, what schemas they return, and what the operating limits are before it acts. The UI step matters in practice too: the engineer debugging why an agent query returned the wrong value on a Tuesday is rarely the same person who configured the OPC UA server, and they need to read the tool schemas without opening a terminal.
